31	> [CLEANUP-PROF] total=125-403ms  tables=76  truncate=123-395ms
32	>                pg_tables=0-18ms  canDisableTriggers=0ms  fixConstraints=1-8ms
33	> Ran 6 tests across 1 file. [3.08s]
34	> ```
35	>
36	> - The `beforeEach` TRUNCATE is **~150ms, not ~4s**. "Truncate only non-empty tables" would save
37	>   ~100ms against a 5s ceiling — it would NOT have fixed the flake. Both of us had assumed it; the
38	>   measurement killed it before either wrote code.
39	> - The dominant cost is the **`beforeAll` at ~1.43s** (spawn embedded Postgres 659ms + run
40	>   migrations 768ms), charged to the FIRST test in the lane.
41	> - Therefore `(unnamed)` is the **first test carrying that beforeAll cost — NOT the beforeEach
42	>   hook**, which is what I originally recorded here and below. Nothing is near 5s on its own.
43	> - `deadlock-retry` / `canDisableTriggers` / `fixConstraints` are all ~0-8ms. Not drivers.
44	>
45	> Real shape: hooks doing legitimate multi-second I/O are subject to the same 5s default as a pure
46	> unit test; 1.43s × contention crosses it. Only remaining evidence-backed fix is raising the hook
47	> ceiling for DB-backed suites. **New-information threshold: cleanup above ~400ms** (baseline
48	> 125-186ms across 76 tables, one 403ms outlier).
49	
50	**The specific flake (2026-08-12, PRs #2687/#2688).** `server-integration-bun` timed out twice at exactly 5000ms:
51	- `UserAuthProfileStore > dropAgent cascades through all secrets`
52	- `OAuthStateStore (Postgres-backed)`
53	
54	Both are Postgres-backed gateway suites. The 3.79s / 4.09s figures often quoted for these are **whole-file wall time, not per-hook cost** — do not reread them as the hook's budget (I did, and it sent me at the TRUNCATE). Per the profile above, the hook that actually approaches the ceiling is the once-per-lane `beforeAll`. They are not broken, they are marginal, so contention tips them over. Three consecutive runs died this way on a CLI-only diff.
55	
56	**The contention source was a peer session.** Check before blaming Depot:
57	
58	```sh
59	for p in $(pgrep -f "run-remote-ci.sh"); do lsof -a -p $p -d cwd -Fn 2>/dev/null | grep ^n; done
60	```
61	
62	More than one path = full CI graphs racing. On 2026-08-12 there were **four** sessions cycling gates (`mcp-app-collapse-generic-returns`, `local-os-files-worker`, `personal-agent-config-drift`, and one in the main checkout). Do **not** kill a peer's run. Either let yours ride (the script's built-in `depot ci retry --failed` sometimes clears it) or wait for a drain. This is the concrete mechanism behind [[feedback_check_for_a_peer_session_on_the_pr_queue]].
63	
64	**A symmetric `until ! pgrep -f run-remote-ci.sh` drain-wait does not solve this — it makes it worse.** If two sessions both queue on drain, they both fire the instant the machine clears and re-collide. Coordinate an explicit order over SendMessage (one session claims the next slot and signals when done) instead of two timers racing.
65	
66	Third suite that crosses the line under load: `UserAuthProfileStore > scanAllOAuth yields every (userId, agentId, organizationId) triple`.
67	
68	Two traps I hit diagnosing it:
69	1. I first concluded "zero jobs report failed" from the summary. Wrong — see above, always go to `attempts[]`.
70	2. Reproducing locally, I ran both suites in one `bun test` invocation. The OAuth one died on a missing `@lobu/connector-worker/compile` build (fresh worktrees need their sibling packages built) and left a **dangling process holding the test DB**, which made the *other* suite's `resetTestDatabase()` hang to 5s. That looked like a confirmed repro and was pure collateral. Run each suite alone before believing a local failure.
71	
72	**FIXED 2026-08-12.** The root cause was not the suites at all: `bunfig.gateway-lane-{1,2}.toml` already declared `timeout = 10000`, but **bun 1.3.5 silently ignores `timeout` in bunfig**, so the lanes ran at the 5s default the whole time while the config looked correct. Fix is the CLI `--timeout` flag at every entry point. Full detail and the controlled probe: [[reference_bun_ignores_timeout_in_bunfig]].
73	
74	Related: [[feedback_piped_make_exit_code_is_a_false_green]], [[feedback_compact_pr_status_and_ci_logs]], [[reference_lobu_cli_runs_dist_not_src]].

content.text:
**Maps feed is built and working.** 213 tests pass (11 new), and against your real archive it parses **383 events**: 27 saved places, 19 reviews, 337 list entries — all with distinct, stable `origin_id`s.

```
saved_place       Veli's Grooming — 472 Caledonian Rd, London N7 8TB
                  lat 51.5483613, lng -0.1178191   ← GeoJSON order, not swapped
place_review      Premier Inn London St Pancras — 1/5
                  Trip type: Vacation / Travel group: Family
saved_list_place  My Cookbook: Fish kievs made with sustainable hake
```

Three traps I pinned with tests: GeoJSON coordinates are `[lon, lat]` (reading positionally puts every London place in the Indian Ocean); list CSVs carry **no date** and the list name exists only in the filename, so file mtime stands in — a fixed sentinel would freeze later list edits out forever; and Google emits a trailing empty row in every list file. I wired it into `lobu.config.ts` too, so it isn't shipped with zero callers.

**What else is in there — ranked by value:**

| source | volume | worth it? |
|---|---|---|
| **My Activity** | 159 files — Search 2MB, Maps 2.7MB, YouTube 2.5MB, **Gemini Apps 166MB** | **Yes.** Your actual behavioural history. Biggest single win. |
| **Google Chat** | 54 files | Yes — real conversations; fits the existing chat-feeds model |
| **Drive** | 961 + 25 + 75 files | Yes, but needs a content strategy (what to index vs skip) |
| **Calendar** | 5 `.ics` | Yes — cheap, and events have clean timestamps |
| **Google Health / Fit** | **2,114** + 126 files | High volume, but is it useful to you? |
| **Contacts** | 1,000 vcards | **Caveat below** |
| **Tasks, Purchases & Reservations, Play Store, Wallet** | small | Cheap wins |
| **Chrome** | 9 files | **Skip** — `History.json` has `Browser History: 0`. Bookmarks/Reading List only. |

Two honest notes so you don't over-invest:

**Contacts looked like the big one and mostly isn't.** I hoped it would fix the duplicate problem — the person resolution policy keys only on email and phone, and just 280/475 of ~5,000 entities have them. But those 1,000 vcards contain only **37 email lines and 136 phone lines**. Mostly names. It'd help at the margin, not solve it.

**"Gemini Apps" is 166MB of the 172MB My Activity total** — that's your entire chat history with Gemini. Whether that's a treasure or noise is your call, and it's the one place I'd want your steer before ingesting.

Confidence: **90** on the Maps feed — parses your real archive correctly with 11 tests and stable ids, but it has *not* been ingested end-to-end through a device worker yet, and no gate has run. **95** on the inventory, counted directly.

Next:
1. E2E the Maps feed through the device worker like I did for twitter/instagram, then gate it.
2. Tell me which of the above to add — I'd start with **My Activity (Search + Maps + YouTube, excluding Gemini)** and **Calendar** as the best value-to-effort.
3. Still queued on Depot behind the peer's bunfig fix — worth having, since `timeout = 10000` was silently ignored by bun and every lane has been running at the 5s default.

**Slot's free — go.** My `run-remote-ci.sh` has exited and marker recorded: `recorded full remote preflight for tree eaa0e4de76d3429e17cd9706fb9918d2ff85650a`.

You get a clean A/B out of this, which is better evidence than either of us had before:

| Run | Conditions | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `nm78zvnhgk` | contended (overlapped your 18-lane run) | `failed=2` → retried → **failed again**, no marker |
| `9dct2qzkw8` | uncontended, **identical tree** `eaa0e4de` | **zero `failed=` lines across all 18 lanes, no retry needed** |

Same tree, same commit, same lanes. The only variable was contention. That's about as close to a controlled experiment as this setup allows, and it independently reproduces your "same tree contended = failed 4x, uncontended = passed first try" measurement on a different diff and a different lane pair.

Worth flagging one asymmetry in the second run: it needed **no retry at all**. My earlier "green" runs today were all failed-then-retried-green. So the uncontended signature isn't just "passes eventually" — it's "passes first try." If you see a run that only goes green on retry, that's still worth a second look even when the marker records; it means something was marginal.

Two smaller things from the last hour:

**A substring grep is not a readiness signal.** I armed a monitor for server boot with `grep -E "...|ready|..."` and it fired on the log line `Skipping config-driven provider "claude" — already registered` — matching **al-ready**-registered. Harmless here, but the same filter shape used as a wait condition would report a server up that isn't. Word-boundary it or match the actual listen line.

**`make dev` leaves port 8657 held after a kill.** The gateway's HTTP proxy binds 8657 separately from 9473, and killing the parent leaves it bound, so the next boot dies with `EADDRINUSE 127.0.0.1:8657` *after* appearing to start normally. If you boot a local gateway, clear both ports and assert zero holders before starting, not just 9473.

Thanks for the collaboration on this — the `needs:`-reduction and reachability framing genuinely changed how I read my own gate, and I'd have merged off a retry-green without it.
</cross-session-message>

- **"why is it mine? doesn't takeout collector automatically do that"** — pushback on over-escalating a decision; expectation that a takeout connector ingests the takeout. - **"any more stuff we can include in the google takeout btw?"** — what other Takeout data could be ingested. 2. **Key Technical Concepts:** - Lobu monorepo, Bun workspace, worktree-per-task via `make task-setup NAME=` - Gate sequence: `make review-fix` → stage by explicit path → `make pre-pr-remote` (Depot, 18 lanes, tree attestation) → commit → `gh pr create` → `make review` (posts required `pi-review`) → `make ui-review` → `gh pr merge --squash --admin` - **`events.entity_ids` is NEVER written by the sync path** — links recovered by JOIN-at-read through `entity_identities` - Entity names use `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` → set only at creation, never self-heal - Entity resolution: `x-lobu-resolution` on `entity_types.metadata_schema`; `discoverEntityResolutionGroups`; `normalizedResolutionRuleKeys` cross-products `rule.fields` - Behavior templates in `packages/server/src/catalog/behavior-templates.ts` - Device workers: `requiredCapability: "os.files"`, `setup_family: device_bound`, `deviceWorkerId` in `defineConnection` - GeoJSON coordinate order `[longitude, latitude]` - Depot CI contention: concurrent runs supersede/cancel each other; bun 1.3.5 silently ignores `timeout` in bunfig 3. **Files and Code Sections:** - **`examples/personal-agent/x-identity.ts`** (worktree `takeout-entity-naming`, staged) Final state after synthesizing my fix with review-fix's: ```ts // Single-segment routes that are shaped exactly like a profile link but are // not one. The anchored pattern below cannot separate `twitter.com/home` from // `twitter.com/jack` structurally — only a list can. // // Deliberately checked HERE and not in `normalizeXHandle`: a real @home or // @intent account exists, and a handle that arrives from tweet metadata rather // than from URL parsing must survive. Only the URL reading is ambiguous. const RESERVED_X_ROUTES = new Set([ "home", "explore", "notifications", "messages", "settings", "compose", "search", "login", "logout", "signup", "privacy", "tos", ]); export function handleFromUserLink( userLink: string | null | undefined ): string | null { if (typeof userLink !== "string") return null; const match = userLink.match( /^https?:\/\/(?:www\.)?(?:twitter|x)\.com\/([^/?#]+)\/?(?:[?#].*)?$/i ); if (!match) return null; const handle = normalizeXHandle(match[1]); return handle && RESERVED_X_ROUTES.has(handle) ? null : handle; } ``` `normalizeXHandle` left permissive (no reserved check) so a real @intent from tweet metadata survives. - **`examples/personal-agent/instagram-takeout.connector.ts`** (staged) ```ts const username = usernameFromProfileUrl(url) ?? undefined; // `following.html` can repeat the profile URL as its anchor text. Use // the resolved handle for display in that case, while preserving real // display names from the other connection files. const displayName = /^https?:\/\//i.test(name) ? (username ?? name) : name; return [ { // Keep source identity based on the original export fields; display // normalization must not cause existing rows to be minted again. origin_id: stableId("ig_connection", [kind, url, name]), ... payload_text: `${kind}: ${displayName}`, author_name: displayName, ``` `IG_CONNECTION_ATTRIBUTIONS` uses `titlePath: "author_name"` — why the URL became the entity name. - **`examples/personal-agent/__tests__/twitter-takeout.connector.test.ts`** — added `handleFromUserLink rejects BARE reserved routes too` test asserting `/home`, `/search?q=x`, `/notifications` → null and `normalizeXHandle("@home") === "home"`. - **`examples/personal-agent/__tests__/instagram-takeout.connector.test.ts`** — added test with realistic fixture `https://www.instagram.com/_u/rampue` asserting `author_name === "rampue"`, plus a test that real display names are preserved verbatim. - **`packages/connector-worker/src/bin.ts`** (worktree `local-os-files-worker`, staged) — reviewer blocker fix: ```ts if (platform && !process.env.WORKER_API_TOKEN?.startsWith('owl_pat_')) { console.error( 'Error: device mode requires a durable personal access token in WORKER_API_TOKEN.\n' + " `lobu whoami --json` falls back to your session's OAuth access token, which\n" + ' expires within 24h and would leave this daemon polling 401 indefinitely.\n' + ' Mint a device token and pass it as WORKER_API_TOKEN (expects an owl_pat_ prefix).' ); process.exit(1); } ``` - **`packages/connector-worker/src/__tests__/device-mode-requires-durable-token.test.ts`** (NEW, staged) — 4 tests spawning the bin against `http://127.0.0.1:1`: no token → fail closed, OAuth token (`ya29.…`) → fail closed, `owl_pat_…` → reaches "Starting worker daemon", fleet (no `--platform`) → unaffected. - **`packages/connector-worker/src/__tests__/device-worker-poll-body.test.ts`** — header compressed from 27 lines to 8 per reviewer request. - **`examples/personal-agent/google-takeout.connector.ts`** (worktree `google-maps-takeout`, NEW WORK, uncommitted) Added `last_maps_timestamp?: string` to checkpoint; `MapsFeature` interface; `maps` feed declaration; sync branch; description updated to mention Maps. New methods: ```ts private readMapsEvents(takeoutDir: string): EventEnvelope[] { return [ ...this.readMapsPlaceFile(takeoutDir, "Saved Places.json", "saved_place"), ...this.readMapsPlaceFile(takeoutDir, "Reviews.json", "place_review"), ...this.readMapsListEvents(takeoutDir), ]; } ``` `readMapsPlaceFile` reads `Maps (your places)/`, requires `location.name`, uses `parseDate(props?.date)`, destructures `const [longitude, latitude] = feature.geometry?.coordinates ?? []`, `origin_id: stableId("google_maps_place", [originType, props?.google_maps_url, name])`. `readMapsListEvents` reads `Saved/*.csv`, list name from filename, `occurredAt` from `statSync(filePath).mtime.toISOString()`, skips blank Title rows, `origin_id: stableId("google_maps_list_place", [listName, title, row.URL])`. Imports added: `statSync` from node:fs; `parseCsv`, `parseDate` from takeout-utils. - **`examples/personal-agent/lobu.config.ts`** (google-maps-takeout worktree) — added: ```ts { feed: "maps", config: takeoutConfig("GOOGLE_MAPS_TAKEOUT_DIR", "google-maps"), }, ``` - **`examples/personal-agent/__tests__/google-maps-takeout.test.ts`** (NEW, 11 tests, all pass) — fixture-based; pins GeoJSON lon/lat order, name-required guard, review rating + questions, list name from filename, mtime-as-date rationale, trailing empty row dropped, origin_id distinct+stable across runs. - **`/private/tmp/claude-501/…/scratchpad/e2e/lobu.config.ts`** — e2e rig config, now has twitter + instagram + google connections, all with `deviceWorkerId: process.env.E2E_DEVICE_WORKER_ID`. 4. **Errors and fixes:** - **Wrong column measured** — I reported "0% attribution" from `events.entity_ids`. `entity-link-upsert.ts:15` says it's never written by design. Corrected to the user explicitly. - **AskUserQuestion rejected** — user wanted to clarify; then asked "don't we have a behavior for it". I had started designing a `find_duplicates` API without checking the catalog. Root fix: grep the behavior catalog first. - **`trigger_feed` 403** — pat.txt was the device-worker PAT (empty scope). Minted a new admin PAT via direct SQL insert (sha256 hash, 12-char prefix); first insert failed on FK because I used the PAT *name* `local-init` as organization_id instead of `org_KMEpsnsTQa0`. - **Twitter re-sync returned 0 items** — checkpoint `last_followers_timestamp` already past the 1970-01-02 stamp. Fixed by `UPDATE feeds SET checkpoint='{}'::jsonb WHERE id=2`. - **Device-bound apply failure** — "pass device_worker_id for one of your devices". Fixed by adding `deviceWorkerId` to `defineConnection` (field exists in `packages/cli/src/config/define.ts:288`). - **review-fix replaced my approach** — dropped `RESERVED_X_HANDLES`, anchored the regex, and flipped my assertion. It caught a real bug in mine (unanchored regex matched `example.com/twitter.com/jack`). I synthesized both rather than reverting. - **`make task-setup` failed** — "branch already used by worktree at personal-agent-config-drift". Fixed by `git restore --source=HEAD --staged --worktree`, switching the old worktree back to `feat/personal-agent-config-drift`, then re-running task-setup. - **New worktree diff showed 3 extra files** — looked like contamination; was actually the branch being 1 commit behind main (#2689). `git status` showing only my 4 files was the discriminator. Fixed with `git merge --ff-only origin/main`. - **Depot gate failures (×4)** — I called it flake, then "infra", then found the real cause: peer Claude sessions running concurrent gates. Also **my own drain-loop was broken**: `pgrep -f "run-remote-ci.sh"` self-matches because the `zsh -c` wrapper's command line contains the literal string. My bounded `for` loop degraded to a fixed ~30-min wait. Correct check: `ps -o pid,etime,command -A | grep "[r]un-remote-ci.sh"`. - **I collided with a peer** — started a gate seconds before their claim arrived; two live runs (PIDs 99655 mine, 6247 theirs). I killed mine (larger remaining work) rather than defend first-start. - **Memory contradictions I wrote and corrected:** I wrote "cancelled = contention, failed = real failure" into memory, contradicting my own note from 16:08 the same day. Peers corrected both halves — neither status classifies. Also corrected: `(unnamed)` is the *first test* carrying a ~1.43s `beforeAll`, NOT the beforeEach hook; TRUNCATE is ~150ms not ~4s. - **Misattributed a peer finding** — credited `/ui-approve` discovery to the wrong session; corrected with both. 5. **Problem Solving:** - **Prod entity repair (DONE, verified):** org `8dc12bdd-5d8c-4768-a2e9-a18005cc5ebd`. Backed up 1126 rows to `entity-repair-backup.tsv` first. Verified no unique constraint on `entities.name` (only `entities_slug_parent_unique`). Single transaction: 824 UPDATE (name = x_user_id identifier, `metadata - 'x_handle'`, aliases filtered), 302 UPDATE (name = ig_username), 1 DELETE from entity_identities. Second transaction: 265 rows with junk `intent` alias stripped. All verification counts now 0. - **Duplicate-merge Behavior (diagnosed, no code):** exists as built-in template, active in prod, runs daily, has done 16 merges. Detection ceiling = person type's 4 rules (email auto_merge, phone review); only 280/475 of ~5,000 entities qualify. Person entities by identity-namespace count: 0:624, **1:3718**, 2:635, 3+:26. 38 people split across `ig_username`/`x_handle`/`linkedin_slug` on identical handle strings. Cross-connector matching unreachable by config due to cross-product semantics. - **Google Maps feed (BUILT, tested, e2e in progress):** 383 events parsed from real archive — 27 saved_place, 19 place_review, 337 saved_list_place, all 383 distinct origin_ids. - **Takeout inventory:** Takeout 2 has 47 subfolders. Unused high-value: My Activity (159 files; Gemini Apps 166MB, Maps 2.7MB, YouTube 2.5MB, Search 2MB), Google Chat (54), Drive (961+25+75), Calendar (5 .ics), Google Health (2114), Fit (126), Contacts (1000 vcards but only 37 email + 136 tel lines), Tasks, Purchases & Reservations. Chrome should be skipped — `History.json` has `Browser History: 0`. 6. **All user messages:** - "fix all properly and make sure instagram etc also works test e2e fix merge" - "cleanup fix and make sure it all works. i want the system to also let me now duplicate entiteies and let me merge etc" - "don't we have a behavior for it" - "you need to operate on the worktrees no?" - "also do we have the google maps pins saved places favourites and everything?" - "why is it mine? doesn't takeout collector automatically do that" - "any more stuff we can include in the google takeout btw?" 7. **Pending Tasks:** - Finish e2e of the Maps feed (trigger the feed, verify events land) - Gate all three branches on Depot (queued behind peer's bunfig fix), push, open PRs, merge - Answer/act on which additional Takeout sources to ingest — I recommended My Activity (Search+Maps+YouTube, excluding Gemini) and Calendar - Duplicates decision: whether to add union semantics to the rule engine (unlocks 38 handle-split people but reverses the template's deliberate "never decide identity from names, aliases, or handles" stance) - Optionally re-trigger duplicate Behavior to re-raise the 10 expired proposals (`expired` doesn't suppress by fingerprint, only `rejected` does) - Tear down local e2e rig (daemon, port 9418, admin PAT minted in dev DB) 8. **Current Work:** E2E'ing the Google Maps feed through the local rig. Verified rig alive (gateway 9418 → 200, 2 connector-worker processes, device worker `e6ce5f2c-8228-44bd-8cfa-b25d1f0715ae`). Copied the new `google-takeout.connector.ts` and `takeout-utils.ts` into the scratchpad e2e dir, added a `googleConnection` (slug `e2e-google-maps`, feed `maps`, `GOOGLE_TAKEOUT_DIR=$HOME/Downloads/Takeout 2`) to the e2e config, and ran apply successfully: ``` + connector-definition google.takeout (installed) + connection e2e-google-maps + feed e2e-google-maps/maps Apply complete. ``` Prior to this: `git status` in `google-maps-takeout` worktree shows `M google-takeout.connector.ts`, `M lobu.config.ts`, `?? __tests__/google-maps-takeout.test.ts`; `git diff --stat origin/main` = 2 files, 184 insertions. Full example suite: **213 pass, 0 fail across 10 files**. Depot slot held by a peer (PID 37800). Two other branches staged and waiting: `local-os-files-worker` (3 files, PR #2687) and `takeout-entity-naming` (4 files, no PR yet). 9. **Optional Next Step:** Trigger the newly created `e2e-google-maps/maps` feed and verify the events land, completing the e2e for the Maps feed — directly continuing the work in flight. The feed id needs looking up, then: `curl -s -X POST http://localhost:9418/api/local-install/manage_feeds -H "Authorization: Bearer $(cat scratchpad/admin-pat.txt)" -d '{"action":"trigger_feed","feed_id":}'`, then verify with `psql -p 5418 -d lobu_feat_local_os_files_worker` that ~383 events landed with `metadata->>'platform'='google_maps'` across the three origin_types. This follows from the user's "why is it mine? doesn't takeout collector automatically do that" (build the Maps feed) and my stated next action: *"E2E the Maps feed through the device worker like I did for twitter/instagram, then gate it."* Confidence stated to the user was **90** on the Maps feed precisely because *"it has **not** been ingested end-to-end through a device worker yet, and no gate has run."* If you need specific details from before compaction (like exact code snippets, error messages, or content you generated), read the full transcript at: /Users/burakemre/.claude/projects/-Users-burakemre-Code-lobu/90d4e325-62fd-4c7c-a94f-fe56982ad059.jsonl Continue the conversation from where it left off without asking the user any further questions. Resume directly — do not acknowledge the summary, do not recap what was happening, do not preface with "I'll continue" or similar. Pick up the last task as if the break never happened.

---
name: reference_depot_cancelled_lanes_hide_a_real_timeout_failure
description: "Depot lanes reporting \"cancelled\" OR a hard \"failed\" are usually peer-session contention tipping ~4s gateway Postgres suites past their 5s timeout — not your diff"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: e3e39998-3947-4d70-b1e6-a73e5b005158
  modified: 2026-08-12T17:06:34.523Z
---

**`failed` does not mean your diff broke something, and `cancelled` does not mean pure infra flake.** Both are usually the same thing: peer-session contention. Measured over 5 runs of one CLI-only diff on 2026-08-12 — contended produced a hard `failed=2`; the identical tree run uncontended passed first try with **no retry**. Do not go bug-hunting on a `failed` lane your diff cannot reach; re-run uncontended first (see the pgrep below).

When `make pre-pr-remote` prints `cancelled` jobs, fail-fast means one attempt genuinely failed and cancelled the siblings. The summary line is actively misleading in two ways:

- `Depot run <id> failed (CLI exit 0)` — the Depot CLI exits 0 on a cancelled workflow, so a piped invocation looks clean.
- The job-level `status` is `cancelled` even for the job that failed; the real signal is one level down in `attempts[].status`.

Find the actual culprit — job names are absent at the top level, so key off attempt status:

```sh
depot ci status <run_id> --org "$DEPOT_ORG_ID" --output json \
  | jq -r '.workflows[0].jobs[] | "\(.status)\t\(.job_key)\t\([.attempts[].status]|join(","))"'
```
The row whose attempts contain `failed` is the cause. Then `depot ci logs <run_id> --org <org> --job <job_key>` — note it wants the **job_key** (`server-integration-bun`), not the `job_id` (`ndbnggvb0f`); passing the id returns "job not found" and helpfully lists the valid keys.

> **CAUSE CORRECTED 2026-08-12 by instrumentation — do not act on the `resetTestDatabase()` theory
> below.** A peer profiled `cleanupTestDatabase()` / `ensureDbForGatewayTests()` directly:
>
> ```
> [INIT-PROF]    startEmbeddedBackend=659ms  setupTestDatabase=768ms   (beforeAll, ONCE per lane)
> [CLEANUP-PROF] total=125-403ms  tables=76  truncate=123-395ms
>                pg_tables=0-18ms  canDisableTriggers=0ms  fixConstraints=1-8ms
> Ran 6 tests across 1 file. [3.08s]
> ```
>
> - The `beforeEach` TRUNCATE is **~150ms, not ~4s**. "Truncate only non-empty tables" would save
>   ~100ms against a 5s ceiling — it would NOT have fixed the flake. Both of us had assumed it; the
>   measurement killed it before either wrote code.
> - The dominant cost is the **`beforeAll` at ~1.43s** (spawn embedded Postgres 659ms + run
>   migrations 768ms), charged to the FIRST test in the lane.
> - Therefore `(unnamed)` is the **first test carrying that beforeAll cost — NOT the beforeEach
>   hook**, which is what I originally recorded here and below. Nothing is near 5s on its own.
> - `deadlock-retry` / `canDisableTriggers` / `fixConstraints` are all ~0-8ms. Not drivers.
>
> Real shape: hooks doing legitimate multi-second I/O are subject to the same 5s default as a pure
> unit test; 1.43s × contention crosses it. Only remaining evidence-backed fix is raising the hook
> ceiling for DB-backed suites. **New-information threshold: cleanup above ~400ms** (baseline
> 125-186ms across 76 tables, one 403ms outlier).

**The specific flake (2026-08-12, PRs #2687/#2688).** `server-integration-bun` timed out twice at exactly 5000ms:
- `UserAuthProfileStore > dropAgent cascades through all secrets`
- `OAuthStateStore (Postgres-backed)`

Both are Postgres-backed gateway suites. The 3.79s / 4.09s figures often quoted for these are **whole-file wall time, not per-hook cost** — do not reread them as the hook's budget (I did, and it sent me at the TRUNCATE). Per the profile above, the hook that actually approaches the ceiling is the once-per-lane `beforeAll`. They are not broken, they are marginal, so contention tips them over. Three consecutive runs died this way on a CLI-only diff.

**The contention source was a peer session.** Check before blaming Depot:

```sh
for p in $(pgrep -f "run-remote-ci.sh"); do lsof -a -p $p -d cwd -Fn 2>/dev/null | grep ^n; done
```

More than one path = full CI graphs racing. On 2026-08-12 there were **four** sessions cycling gates (`mcp-app-collapse-generic-returns`, `local-os-files-worker`, `personal-agent-config-drift`, and one in the main checkout). Do **not** kill a peer's run. Either let yours ride (the script's built-in `depot ci retry --failed` sometimes clears it) or wait for a drain. This is the concrete mechanism behind [[feedback_check_for_a_peer_session_on_the_pr_queue]].

**A symmetric `until ! pgrep -f run-remote-ci.sh` drain-wait does not solve this — it makes it worse.** If two sessions both queue on drain, they both fire the instant the machine clears and re-collide. Coordinate an explicit order over SendMessage (one session claims the next slot and signals when done) instead of two timers racing.

Third suite that crosses the line under load: `UserAuthProfileStore > scanAllOAuth yields every (userId, agentId, organizationId) triple`.

Two traps I hit diagnosing it:
1. I first concluded "zero jobs report failed" from the summary. Wrong — see above, always go to `attempts[]`.
2. Reproducing locally, I ran both suites in one `bun test` invocation. The OAuth one died on a missing `@lobu/connector-worker/compile` build (fresh worktrees need their sibling packages built) and left a **dangling process holding the test DB**, which made the *other* suite's `resetTestDatabase()` hang to 5s. That looked like a confirmed repro and was pure collateral. Run each suite alone before believing a local failure.

**FIXED 2026-08-12.** The root cause was not the suites at all: `bunfig.gateway-lane-{1,2}.toml` already declared `timeout = 10000`, but **bun 1.3.5 silently ignores `timeout` in bunfig**, so the lanes ran at the 5s default the whole time while the config looked correct. Fix is the CLI `--timeout` flag at every entry point. Full detail and the controlled probe: [[reference_bun_ignores_timeout_in_bunfig]].

Related: [[feedback_piped_make_exit_code_is_a_false_green]], [[feedback_compact_pr_status_and_ci_logs]], [[reference_lobu_cli_runs_dist_not_src]].

<!-- Per-repo agent rules loaded into every Claude Code session in this repo. Inlines AGENTS.md (shared project rules) first, then layers local-only notes below. User memory entries live under ~/.claude/projects/.../memory/. Don't add anything here unless it's only relevant to Claude agent specific. If other harnesses like pi or codex need it, modify AGENTS.md -->

@AGENTS.md

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- frontend-typescript-tailwind: Use this agent when you need to develop frontend applications or components using TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and shadcn/ui. This includes creating React components, implementing UI designs, setting up frontend projects, refactoring existing frontend code to follow best practices, or solving frontend-specific issues. The agent specializes in modern frontend development patterns and component-based architecture.

Examples:
- <example>
  Context: The user needs to create a new React component with TypeScript and Tailwind.
  user: "Create a card component that displays user information"
  assistant: "I'll use the frontend-typescript-tailwind agent to create a properly typed React component with Tailwind styling following best practices."
  <commentary>
  Since the user is asking for frontend component creation, use the frontend-typescript-tailwind agent to ensure TypeScript types, Tailwind classes, and shadcn/ui patterns are properly implemented.
  </commentary>
</example>
- <example>
  Context: The user wants to refactor existing frontend code.
  user: "Can you review and improve this dashboard component to use better TypeScript types and Tailwind conventions?"
  assistant: "I'll use the frontend-typescript-tailwind agent to analyze and refactor your dashboard component following TypeScript and Tailwind best practices."
  <commentary>
  The user is asking for frontend code improvement, so the frontend-typescript-tailwind agent should be used to ensure proper typing and styling conventions.
  </commentary>
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- mvp-architect-k8s: Use this agent when you need to architect and develop an MVP (Minimum Viable Product) with a focus on cloud-native infrastructure using Kubernetes, Cloudflare services, and maintaining high code quality standards. This includes setting up deployments, configuring DNS/CDN, implementing CI/CD pipelines, and monitoring code complexity. Examples:

<example>
Context: User needs help setting up a new MVP project with proper infrastructure.
user: "I need to create a new web application MVP with proper deployment setup"
assistant: "I'll use the Task tool to launch the mvp-architect-k8s agent to help architect and set up your MVP with Kubernetes, Cloudflare, and proper CI/CD."
<commentary>
Since the user needs MVP development with infrastructure setup, use the mvp-architect-k8s agent to handle the architecture and deployment configuration.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: User wants to deploy their application to Kubernetes with proper domain setup.
user: "Deploy my app to Kubernetes and configure the domain with CDN"
assistant: "Let me use the Task tool to launch the mvp-architect-k8s agent to handle the Kubernetes deployment and Cloudflare configuration."
<commentary>
The user needs Kubernetes deployment and Cloudflare setup, which are core competencies of the mvp-architect-k8s agent.
</commentary>
</example>

## computer-use
You have a computer-use MCP available (tools named `mcp__computer-use__*`). It lets you take screenshots of the user's desktop and control it with mouse clicks, keyboard input, and scrolling.

**Pick the right tool for the app.** Each tier trades speed/precision against coverage:

1. **Dedicated MCP for the app** — if the task is in an app that has its own MCP (Slack, Gmail, Calendar, Linear, etc.) and that MCP is connected, use it. API-backed tools are fast and precise.
2. **Chrome MCP** (`mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`) — if the target is a web app and there's no dedicated MCP for it, use the browser tools. DOM-aware, much faster than clicking pixels. If the Chrome extension isn't connected, ask the user to install it rather than falling through to computer use.
3. **Computer use** — for native desktop apps (Maps, Notes, Finder, Photos, System Settings, any third-party native app) and cross-app workflows. Computer use IS the right tool here — don't decline a native-app task just because there's no dedicated MCP for it.

This is about what's available, not error handling — if a dedicated MCP tool errors, debug or report it rather than silently retrying via a slower tier.

**Look before you assert.** If the user asks about app state (what's open, what's connected, what an app can do), take a screenshot and check before answering. Don't answer from memory — the user's setup or app version may differ from what you expect. If you're about to say an app doesn't support an action, that claim should be grounded in what you just saw on screen, not general knowledge. Similarly, `list_granted_applications` or a fresh `screenshot` is cheaper than a wrong assertion about what's running.

**Loading via ToolSearch — load in bulk, not one-by-one:** if computer-use tools are in the deferred list, load them ALL in a single ToolSearch call: `{ query: "computer-use", max_results: 30 }`. The keyword search matches the server-name substring in every tool name, so one query returns the entire toolkit. Don't use `select:` for individual tools — that's one round-trip per tool.

**Access flow:** before any computer-use action you must call `request_access` with the list of applications you need. The user approves each application explicitly, and you may need to call it again mid-task if you discover you need another application.

**Tiered apps:** some apps are granted at a restricted tier based on their category — the tier is displayed in the approval dialog and returned in the `request_access` response:
- **Browsers** (Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Arc, etc.) → tier **"read"**: visible in screenshots, but clicks and typing are blocked. You can read what's already on screen. For navigation, clicking, or form-filling, use the claude-in-chrome MCP (tools named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`; load via ToolSearch if deferred).
- **Terminals and IDEs** (Terminal, iTerm, VS Code, JetBrains, etc.) → tier **"click"**: visible and left-clickable, but typing, key presses, right-click, modifier-clicks, and drag-drop are blocked. You can click a Run button or scroll test output, but cannot type into the editor or integrated terminal, cannot right-click (the context menu has Paste), and cannot drag text onto them. For shell commands, use the Bash tool.
- **Everything else** → tier **"full"**: no restrictions.

The tier is enforced by the frontmost-app check: if a tier-"read" app is in front, `left_click` returns an error; if a tier-"click" app is in front, `type` and `right_click` return errors. The error tells you what tier the app has and what to do instead. `open_application` works at any tier — bringing an app forward is a read-level operation.

**Link safety — treat links in emails and messages as suspicious by default.**
- **Never click web links with computer-use tools.** If you encounter a link in a native app (Mail, Messages, a PDF, etc.), do NOT `left_click` it. Open the URL via the claude-in-chrome MCP instead.
- **See the full URL before following any link.** Visible link text can be misleading — hover or inspect to get the real destination.
- **Links from emails, messages, or unknown-sender documents are suspicious by default.** If the destination URL is at all unfamiliar or looks off, ask the user for confirmation before proceeding.
- **Inside the Chrome extension** you can click links with the extension's tools, but the suspicion check still applies — verify unfamiliar URLs with the user.

**Financial actions - do not execute trades or move money.** Budgeting and accounting apps (Quicken, YNAB, QuickBooks, etc.) are granted at full tier so you can categorize transactions, generate reports, and help the user organize their finances. But never execute a trade, place an order, send money, or initiate a transfer on the user's behalf - always ask the user to perform those actions themselves.

## context7
Use this server to fetch current documentation whenever the user asks about a library, framework, SDK, API, CLI tool, or cloud service — even well-known ones like React, Next.js, Prisma, Express, Tailwind, Django, or Spring Boot. This includes API syntax, configuration, version migration, library-specific debugging, setup instructions, and CLI tool usage. Use even when you think you know the answer — your training data may not reflect recent changes. Prefer this over web search for library docs.

Do not use for: refactoring, writing scripts from scratch, debugging business logic, code review, or general programming concepts.

## pencil
The Pencil MCP server is the editor for .pen design files (web/mobile apps and websites). Use it to read, generate, and validate designs.

.pen files are encrypted: access them only via "pencil" MCP tools — never use Read or Grep on .pen files. Follow each tool's input schema exactly.

Always call get_app_state({ include_schema: true, include_canvas_design: true, include_scripts_and_shaders: false }) if you don't have the current .pen file schema in the context. All three flags are required. Knowing the schema is required to use any other Pencil MCP tool.

Tools: get_app_state, get_guidelines, execute, get_screenshot, export_nodes, export_html.

That's about as close to a controlled experiment as this setup allows, and it independently reproduces your "same tree contended = failed 4x, uncontended = passed first try" measurement on a different diff and a different lane pair.

Worth flagging one asymmetry in the second run: it needed **no retry at all**. My earlier "green" runs today were all failed-then-retried-green. So the uncontended signature isn't just "passes eventually" — it's "passes first try." If you see a run that only goes green on retry, that's still worth a second look even when the marker records; it means something was marginal.

Two smaller things from the last hour:

**A substring grep is not a readiness signal.** I armed a monitor for server boot with `grep -E "...|ready|..."` and it fired on the log line `Skipping config-driven provider "claude" — already registered` — matching **al-ready**-registered. Harmless here, but the same filter shape used as a wait condition would report a server up that isn't. Word-boundary it or match the actual listen line.

**`make dev` leaves port 8657 held after a kill.** The gateway's HTTP proxy binds 8657 separately from 9473, and killing the parent leaves it bound, so the next boot dies with `EADDRINUSE 127.0.0.1:8657` *after* appearing to start normally. If you boot a local gateway, clear both ports and assert zero holders before starting, not just 9473.

Thanks for the collaboration on this — the `needs:`-reduction and reachability framing genuinely changed how I read my own gate, and I'd have merged off a retry-green without it.
</cross-session-message>

## Repo map
- Bun workspace under `packages/*`; TS source is in `src`, tests in `__tests__`.
- Main packages: `core` shared types/utils, `plugin-api` native plugin contracts, `plugin-host` deterministic plugin composition, `server` gateway + embedded runtime, `agent-worker` Lobu agent execution, `connectors` built-in connectors, `owletto` frontend submodule.
- Before editing a package, read its nearest `AGENTS.md` if present.
- `docs/GOTCHAS.md` collects the mechanical traps (build, SQL, testing, submodule, browser) that have each cost a debugging session. Skim the section for the surface you are touching before you start, and grep it when something looks inexplicable.

## Hard invariants
- **Never write to `~/Code/lobu` directly — work in a worktree.** Run `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` first, and never `git switch` in the main checkout.
- One branch = one concern (not one file). Tangential task → commit/push/open current work, then branch fresh from `main`. Split only for genuinely independent concerns or an unreviewable diff.
- **Multi-replica correctness is mandatory.** Never put shared required state in an in-memory Map/singleton another replica must read or mutate. If a feature relies on cross-pod visibility, use Postgres-mediated state/signal.
- **`events` is append-only.** Never `DELETE FROM events`; tombstone/supersede instead.
- **`events.id` is a stored-version id, not stable source identity.** Connector resyncs can supersede a row and allocate a new id for the same source item. Cross-sync identity and dedupe must use the connector's stable `origin_id` (scoped to its connection/source) or an explicit domain key, never `events.id`.
- **Request paths never aggregate history.** No `GROUP BY`, `DISTINCT ON`, per-row `regexp_*`, or leading-wildcard `LIKE` over an append-only / run-history table (`events`, `agent_transcript_snapshot`, `session_calls`, …) on a user-facing read path. History only grows, so read-time aggregation cost grows with it while the answer stays bounded. Materialize the row or counter at WRITE time and read it back by index; run the one-time aggregation in a migration, never per request. Aggregating bounded config tables (`connections`, `watchers`, `agent_users`) is fine.
- **Never bulk-delete prod `organization` rows**, including zero-activity ones — empty-looking orgs are frequently real human signups. Surface them one at a time for confirmation.
- **Workers never receive real credentials.** They may receive only placeholders/proxied access. The only exceptions are device-pinned connectors and short-lived provider-derived credential leases (see `packages/server/AGENTS.md`); a durable stored credential is never one of them.
- Default to static `import`. New dynamic imports require measured cost justification here or in the package AGENTS plus a rationale comment at the call site. Tests may dynamically import after mocks.
  - Node-version gate exceptions: `packages/cli/bin/lobu.js` defers the existing CLI graph without duplicating it, and `packages/server/src/server-entry.ts` adds an 842-byte gate in front of the 4.34 MB server graph (measured 2026-07-24). Both call sites must stay dependency-free until their checks pass.
- Bug fixes require red→fix→green evidence, with both outputs pasted into the PR body. If you cannot reproduce, stop and report the dead end — do not ship a speculative fix.
- Mutation checks require proof that the mutation landed: assert the old pattern exists, verify a countable source change, and confirm the focused test fails before restoring the fix and rerunning green. A green test after a no-op mutation proves nothing.
- Never report done off a green typecheck. Boot it, exercise every branch you touched, clean up test data. If "compiles" is all you ran, say so explicitly.
- Gates are non-negotiable (sequence in "Ship a change" below). `make pre-pr-remote` runs the full Linux CI graph on Depot against the staged tree and builds before checks that consume dist — that build step protects against a stale-dist false green. `make pre-pr` is the CPU-heavy local fallback. `make review` is an LLM verdict only: it does NOT run typecheck/knip/tests and is not proof CI will pass.
- The agent-facing product name is **Behavior**; `watcher` is internal engine/DB vocabulary. It must not appear in MCP tool schemas/names/descriptions, ClientSDK discovery metadata, or the connector-sdk public reaction contract — `make pre-pr-remote` fails on it. Internal identifiers (`actingWatcherId`, table/column names, comments) are fine.
- `make review-fix` is the unposted fixer pass and runs BEFORE the first `make review`; verify its diff and commit it. Never iterate `make review` as a find-fix loop — each posted round costs a review + CI cycle.
- **A UI change owes visual proof.** For an Owletto pointer PR, `make ui-review` publishes the before/after comparison on the exact merged Owletto PR and links it from the parent. Publishing the proof is what the gate asserts — review it like any other change on the PR. A changed pointer republishes it.
- Fix the class, not the instance: on the first hit, grep every other instance and fix in one pass — a diff-scoped reviewer only ever finds the next one. Same root cause twice = stop reviewing, grep-enumerate. A class-wide fix is in scope for the branch that found it and does not count as scope creep.
- **Fail closed on durable dispatch/delivery state.** When a durable coordination or delivery operation fails, its caller must not reinterpret the error as proceed/deliver/skip. Propagate a retry, defer, or terminal-failure outcome with a visible log; if the operation may already have succeeded, reconcile idempotently before retrying. Treat lock timeouts, pool errors, and ambiguous or expired rows as failures, not as "nothing changed."
- **Coordination design brake.** A change that needs a second lock, a second retry/deferral budget, or a prose termination argument to explain why it halts is patching a misplaced check — stop and re-derive where the decision belongs before adding mechanism. Find the chokepoint that already serializes the action (e.g. worker dispatch is serialized by `job-router` on the worker-SSE-owner pod) and put the check there; prefer deleting the state transition over coordinating it, and reuse queue-native retry over hand-rolled hold/requeue.
- **Stage by explicit path; never commit the whole tree of a worktree that hosted other work.** A commit is a snapshot — stale file copies silently revert already-merged PRs. After commit/rebase, `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` must equal the task's intended file list; extra files = stop. Verify a "reverts merged work" review finding by diff direction against `origin/main`, never dismiss it as merge-base noise.

## Ship a change
1. `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` → work in `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/`.
2. Reproduce the bug (red) before fixing it. Fix, then prove green.
3. Iterate with focused local tests: one file via `bun test <path>`, or `cd packages/server && bunx vitest run <path>` for vitest suites. Use `make pre-pr-remote-fast` when broad required-gate confidence is useful before the diff settles; it runs remotely and never substitutes for the final full gate.
4. `make review-fix` on the settled diff and verify what it changed — it edits the working tree, so re-read the files before trusting them.
5. Stage every intended file by explicit path (`git add -- <paths>`, never `-A`), then `make pre-pr-remote` to run the full staged Linux CI graph on Depot. It fails closed on untracked or unstaged changes so the successful tree attestation survives the following commit. The macOS app lane remains on GitHub/Mac hardware. Use the CPU-heavy local `make pre-pr` only when Depot is unavailable; intentional workflow/action changes require `DEPOT_ALLOW_WORKFLOW_CHANGES=1 make pre-pr-remote` after review.
6. Commit, then confirm `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` is exactly your intended file list. Extra files = stop.
7. `git push -u origin <branch>` → `gh pr create` (fill `.github/pull_request_template.md`; conventional-commit title, e.g. `fix(server): …`).
8. `make review` **once** on the settled HEAD. It posts the `pi-review` status, which is a REQUIRED check. Small safe-class diffs (docs/renames/generated/additive-tests, <100 lines) skip the cross-harness reviewer by default; run `REVIEWER_MODE=full make review` to force the independent review, and `REVIEWER_SHADOW=1` to measure the skip rule instead of trusting it.
9. `make ui-review`. It passes non-Owletto changes as not applicable. For an Owletto pointer change, run `ARTIFACT=<hosted-html-url> make ui-review`; it publishes the before/after proof on the exact merged Owletto PR, links it from the parent, and passes. No `ARTIFACT` means no proof and no pass.
10. Merge squash once CI is green: `gh pr merge <n> --squash --admin`. Never `--admin` past a check that has not reported.
11. Prod-visible surface? Verify it live after rollout. Set a self-rescheduling `ScheduleWakeup` (~1500s) carrying the rollout gate: poll the deployed SHA, then `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$MERGE_SHA" "$DEPLOYED_SHA"` with `MERGE_SHA=$(gh pr view <n> --json mergeCommit --jq .mergeCommit.oid)`. Two ways this gate silently never opens — **gate on the squash commit, not your branch head** (a squash merge writes a new commit with no ancestry link to the branch, so the branch head exits 1 forever: PR #2280 has identical trees and still fails), and **keep that argument order** (merge commit first; reversed, it accepts a stale deploy). Run the live check when it lands, and write the result back to memory.

## Agent workflow
- Do only what was asked. Delete ephemeral files you create. Do not create `*.md` unless asked.
- Never introduce a new table or change the database design, API surface, or SDK surface without explicitly surfacing the proposal and receiving user confirmation first.
- Prefer `bun`; do not use npm/yarn/pnpm for repo work.
- Fix unused params by deleting them, not `_`-prefixing.
- Never `git stash`; use WIP commits and squash later.
- Never resolve merge conflicts in the GitHub web UI (it has silently dropped 1000+ lines of feature work). Rebase locally against `origin/main`, then diff against the last real feature commit before squashing — except on submodule-pointer branches, where you must `git merge` (see `docs/GOTCHAS.md`, "Submodule & cross-repo").
- Run mandated gates automatically; never ask permission to run one.
- Show the diff, not a summary. Before claiming done — on your own work or a dispatched agent's — surface `git status` plus `git diff --stat <base>...HEAD`. An agent's self-report is a claim; the diff is the evidence.
- UI PRs owe before/after screenshots, and `gh` cannot upload images inline. Capture before shots from the unmodified branch and after shots from the same booted app (auth recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`), base64-embed the PNGs into one self-contained HTML comparison page, publish it as a claude.ai artifact, and pass that URL as `ARTIFACT` to `make ui-review`. - `docs/GOTCHAS.md` collects the mechanical traps (build, SQL, testing, submodule, browser) that have each cost a debugging session. Skim the section for the surface you are touching before you start, and grep it when something looks inexplicable.

- **`events.id` is a stored-version id, not stable source identity.** Connector resyncs can supersede a row and allocate a new id for the same source item. History only grows, so read-time aggregation cost grows with it while the answer stays bounded. Materialize the row or counter at WRITE time and read it back by index; run the one-time aggregation in a migration, never per request. input.content:
---
name: feedback_a_wait_condition_that_cannot_report_failure_is_decorative
description: "Before arming any wait/readiness/drain check, ask what it prints if the thing already FAILED and if it already SUCCEEDED — same answer means the check confirms nothing"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
---

**The test, before arming any wait condition:** what would this print if the thing had already *failed*, and what would it print if it had already *succeeded*? **If either answer is the same, the check is decorative** — it will confirm nothing and you will read its silence as progress.

Three instances hit within one afternoon (2026-08-12), by two sessions independently, all the same shape — **matching on a remembered constant instead of observing the running system**:

| Check | Failure mode | Looked like |
|---|---|---|
| `grep -E "\|ready\|"` as a server-boot signal | matched the log line `Skipping … — al**ready** registered` | server up, wasn't |
| poll port `9473` for readiness | that worktree's gateway binds **9414** (task-setup allocates per worktree) | BOOT-FAIL forever while healthy and serving 200s |
| `pgrep -f "run-remote-ci.sh"` as a drain-wait | **self-matched** the invoking shell's own argv | never saw a clear machine; bounded wait silently degraded to a fixed ~30min sleep |

The pgrep one is the worst class: structurally incapable of ever reporting the success state, and it *degraded into a plausible-looking wait* rather than erroring.

**The pgrep claim is invocation-shaped, not universal.** I first recorded it as "pgrep -f self-matches, full stop." A peer disproved that with a control probe:

```sh
pgrep -f "ZZUNIQUEPROBE-run-remote-ci.sh"   # no match — control
pgrep -f "run-remote-ci.sh"                 # only the real process
```

It self-matches when the pattern is in the *invoking* process's argv — i.e. wrapped in `zsh -c '<script text>'` (my harness) — and not when exec'd directly (theirs). ---
name: reference_depot_cancelled_lanes_hide_a_real_timeout_failure
description: "Depot lanes reporting \"cancelled\" OR a hard \"failed\" are usually peer-session contention tipping ~4s gateway Postgres suites past their 5s timeout — not your diff"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: e3e39998-3947-4d70-b1e6-a73e5b005158
  modified: 2026-08-12T17:06:34.523Z
---

**`failed` does not mean your diff broke something, and `cancelled` does not mean pure infra flake.** Both are usually the same thing: peer-session contention. Measured over 5 runs of one CLI-only diff on 2026-08-12 — contended produced a hard `failed=2`; the identical tree run uncontended passed first try with **no retry**. Do not go bug-hunting on a `failed` lane your diff cannot reach; re-run uncontended first (see the pgrep below).

When `make pre-pr-remote` prints `cancelled` jobs, fail-fast means one attempt genuinely failed and cancelled the siblings. The summary line is actively misleading in two ways:

- `Depot run <id> failed (CLI exit 0)` — the Depot CLI exits 0 on a cancelled workflow, so a piped invocation looks clean.
- The job-level `status` is `cancelled` even for the job that failed; the real signal is one level down in `attempts[].status`.

Find the actual culprit — job names are absent at the top level, so key off attempt status:

```sh
depot ci status <run_id> --org "$DEPOT_ORG_ID" --output json \
  | jq -r '.workflows[0].jobs[] | "\(.status)\t\(.job_key)\t\([.attempts[].status]|join(","))"'
```
The row whose attempts contain `failed` is the cause. Then `depot ci logs <run_id> --org <org> --job <job_key>` — note it wants the **job_key** (`server-integration-bun`), not the `job_id` (`ndbnggvb0f`); passing the id returns "job not found" and helpfully lists the valid keys.

> **CAUSE CORRECTED 2026-08-12 by instrumentation — do not act on the `resetTestDatabase()` theory
> below.** A peer profiled `cleanupTestDatabase()` / `ensureDbForGatewayTests()` directly:
>
> ```
> [INIT-PROF]    startEmbeddedBackend=659ms  setupTestDatabase=768ms   (beforeAll, ONCE per lane)
> [CLEANUP-PROF] total=125-403ms  tables=76  truncate=123-395ms
>                pg_tables=0-18ms  canDisableTriggers=0ms  fixConstraints=1-8ms
> Ran 6 tests across 1 file. [3.08s]
> ```
>
> - The `beforeEach` TRUNCATE is **~150ms, not ~4s**. "Truncate only non-empty tables" would save
>   ~100ms against a 5s ceiling — it would NOT have fixed the flake. Both of us had assumed it; the
>   measurement killed it before either wrote code.
> - The dominant cost is the **`beforeAll` at ~1.43s** (spawn embedded Postgres 659ms + run
>   migrations 768ms), charged to the FIRST test in the lane.
> - Therefore `(unnamed)` is the **first test carrying that beforeAll cost — NOT the beforeEach
>   hook**, which is what I originally recorded here and below. Nothing is near 5s on its own.
> - `deadlock-retry` / `canDisableTriggers` / `fixConstraints` are all ~0-8ms. Not drivers.
>
> Real shape: hooks doing legitimate multi-second I/O are subject to the same 5s default as a pure
> unit test; 1.43s × contention crosses it. Only remaining evidence-backed fix is raising the hook
> ceiling for DB-backed suites. **New-information threshold: cleanup above ~400ms** (baseline
> 125-186ms across 76 tables, one 403ms outlier).

**The specific flake (2026-08-12, PRs #2687/#2688).** `server-integration-bun` timed out twice at exactly 5000ms:
- `UserAuthProfileStore > dropAgent cascades through all secrets`
- `OAuthStateStore (Postgres-backed)`

Both are Postgres-backed gateway suites. The 3.79s / 4.09s figures often quoted for these are **whole-file wall time, not per-hook cost** — do not reread them as the hook's budget (I did, and it sent me at the TRUNCATE). Per the profile above, the hook that actually approaches the ceiling is the once-per-lane `beforeAll`. They are not broken, they are marginal, so contention tips them over. Three consecutive runs died this way on a CLI-only diff.

**The contention source was a peer session.** Check before blaming Depot:

```sh
for p in $(pgrep -f "run-remote-ci.sh"); do lsof -a -p $p -d cwd -Fn 2>/dev/null | grep ^n; done
```

More than one path = full CI graphs racing. On 2026-08-12 there were **four** sessions cycling gates (`mcp-app-collapse-generic-returns`, `local-os-files-worker`, `personal-agent-config-drift`, and one in the main checkout). Do **not** kill a peer's run. Either let yours ride (the script's built-in `depot ci retry --failed` sometimes clears it) or wait for a drain. This is the concrete mechanism behind [[feedback_check_for_a_peer_session_on_the_pr_queue]].

**A symmetric `until ! pgrep -f run-remote-ci.sh` drain-wait does not solve this — it makes it worse.** If two sessions both queue on drain, they both fire the instant the machine clears and re-collide. Coordinate an explicit order over SendMessage (one session claims the next slot and signals when done) instead of two timers racing.

Third suite that crosses the line under load: `UserAuthProfileStore > scanAllOAuth yields every (userId, agentId, organizationId) triple`.

Two traps I hit diagnosing it:
1. I first concluded "zero jobs report failed" from the summary. Wrong — see above, always go to `attempts[]`.
2. Reproducing locally, I ran both suites in one `bun test` invocation. The OAuth one died on a missing `@lobu/connector-worker/compile` build (fresh worktrees need their sibling packages built) and left a **dangling process holding the test DB**, which made the *other* suite's `resetTestDatabase()` hang to 5s. That looked like a confirmed repro and was pure collateral. Run each suite alone before believing a local failure.

**FIXED 2026-08-12.** The root cause was not the suites at all: `bunfig.gateway-lane-{1,2}.toml` already declared `timeout = 10000`, but **bun 1.3.5 silently ignores `timeout` in bunfig**, so the lanes ran at the 5s default the whole time while the config looked correct. Fix is the CLI `--timeout` flag at every entry point. Full detail and the controlled probe: [[reference_bun_ignores_timeout_in_bunfig]].

Related: [[feedback_piped_make_exit_code_is_a_false_green]], [[feedback_compact_pr_status_and_ci_logs]], [[reference_lobu_cli_runs_dist_not_src]].

## Summary

Two takeout connectors were minting person entities whose **name is a URL** instead of a handle, because the entity name comes from `author_name` and both connectors were passing raw export text through.

- **Instagram** — `following.html` repeats the profile URL as its own anchor text, so `author_name` became `https://www.instagram.com/_u/rampue`. Entity names use `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, so a name set at creation **never self-heals**; every one of these was permanent. Now a URL-shaped anchor falls back to the resolved handle, while real display names from the other connection files pass through verbatim.
- **X/Twitter** — `handleFromUserLink` accepted any single-segment path, so `twitter.com/home`, `/search`, `/notifications` minted people named `home`, `search`, `notifications`. Those routes are structurally indistinguishable from a profile link, so a reserved-route list is the only thing that can separate them.

Two deliberate scope limits, both load-bearing:

- The reserved check lives in `handleFromUserLink`, **not** in `normalizeXHandle`. A real `@home` / `@intent` account exists; a handle arriving from tweet metadata must survive. Only the *URL reading* is ambiguous.
- `origin_id` still hashes the **original** export fields. Display normalization must not re-mint rows that already exist.

## Test plan
- [x] Intended files staged explicitly, then `make pre-pr-remote` clean (full Linux CI graph on Depot)
- [x] Tests run: `bun test examples/personal-agent/__tests__/` → **207 pass, 0 fail** (9 files)
- [x] Bug fix: red→fix→green outputs pasted below
- [ ] If bot behavior: n/a

```
$ grep -n 'const displayName' instagram-takeout.connector.ts
413:        const displayName = /^https?:\/\//i.test(name)
$ grep -n 'RESERVED_X_ROUTES.has' x-identity.ts
95:  return handle && RESERVED_X_ROUTES.has(handle) ? null : handle;

# mutate: displayName -> raw anchor text; handleFromUserLink -> no reserved check

expect(row.author_name).toBe("rampue");
Expected: "rampue"
Received: "https://www.instagram.com/_u/rampue"
(fail) a following row whose visible text is a URL is named by handle

expect(handleFromUserLink("https://twitter.com/home")).toBe(null);
Expected: null
Received: "home"
(fail) handleFromUserLink rejects BARE reserved routes too

 25 pass
 2 fail
Ran 27 tests across 2 files.
```

### green (fixes restored, tree byte-identical to staged)

```
 207 pass
 0 fail
 664 expect() calls
Ran 207 tests across 9 files. [242.00ms]
```

## Notes

The ~1,100 already-corrupted prod rows were repaired separately by direct SQL (backed up first); this PR stops new ones being minted. `handleFromUserLink`'s regex is also anchored here — the previous pattern was unanchored and matched `example.com/twitter.com/jack`.

Red→green captured for both branches, PR body drafted. Status while the queue drains:

**Google Maps feed — e2e PASSED.** Run 434 completed through the device worker, `items_collected: 383`, checkpoint advanced:

| origin_type | count | range |
|---|---|---|
| `saved_list_place` | 337 | 2021-09-26 → 2026-06-03 |
| `saved_place` | 27 | 2015-09-09 → 2026-03-18 |
| `place_review` | 19 | 2017-03-12 → 2026-05-25 |

Coordinates landed in the right order — `Veli's Grooming` at lat `51.5483613` / lon `-0.1178191` is London, not the Indian Ocean. Reviews carry rating (`— 5/5`), lists carry their name from the filename (`Want to go: Nazaré`).

**Mutation checks — both branches genuinely red before green:**
- `takeout-entity-naming`: mutating out the two fixes produced `Received: "https://www.instagram.com/_u/rampue"` and `Received: "home"`. Restored → 207 pass, tree byte-identical to staged.
- `local-os-files-worker`: mutating the durable-token guard let the OAuth-token case reach `Starting worker daemon`. Restored → 67 pass.

**Depot queue.** The slot was *not* free when I looked — a fourth session (`test-db-cleanup-speed`) took it 39s after the broadcast, and it turns out to be the flake fix itself gating with `DEPOT_ALLOW_WORKFLOW_CHANGES=1`. They asked for one run for `feat/apply-plan-values` before my three; I yielded, since one run against three isn't close and theirs is user-requested work my detour helped delay. My wait is a `ps`-based poll on the machine rather than a trust-the-signal handoff, so it holds regardless.

I also overstated the `pgrep` finding to a peer and corrected it: it self-matches only when the pattern is in the *invoking* shell's argv (my `zsh -c` wrapper), not universally — their control probe disproved the general claim, and their earlier drains were real.

One thing worth your attention on **#2687**: every required check passes except `pi-review`, which failed with 1 blocker — that's the durable-token blocker I've since fixed but not yet pushed. So it needs the gate, a push, and a fresh `make review`, not just a merge.

Confidence:
- **Maps feed — 92.** Parsed, unit-tested (11 tests), and ingested end-to-end through a real device worker against the real archive. Not yet gated on Depot, and `review-fix` is still running on it, so the diff may still change.
- **takeout-entity-naming — 88.** Mutation-verified red→green, full example suite green, prod rows already repaired. No Depot gate yet.
- **local-os-files-worker — 85.** Mutation-verified, 67 tests green, 8/9 required checks already passing on the PR. The one failing check is the thing I fixed, which is exactly the claim the next gate has to prove.

Next actions:
1. Take the slot when `apply-plan-values` exits and gate the three serially — holding "clean first try, no internal retry" as the pass bar, since retry-green is the marginal signature that caused today's confusion.
2. After #2687's push, re-run `make review` once and confirm the blocker clears rather than assuming the fix satisfies it.
3. Run the two-concurrent-runs experiment once the flake fix merges — if both pass first try, we drop the three-way queue protocol entirely.
4. Tear down the local e2e rig (daemon, port 9418, the admin PAT I minted in the dev DB) once the Maps branch is merged.

## Summary

Two takeout connectors were minting person entities whose **name is a URL** instead of a handle, because the entity name comes from `author_name` and both connectors were passing raw export text through.

- **Instagram** — `following.html` repeats the profile URL as its own anchor text, so `author_name` became `https://www.instagram.com/_u/rampue`. Entity names use `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, so a name set at creation **never self-heals**; every one of these was permanent. Now a URL-shaped anchor falls back to the resolved handle, while real display names from the other connection files pass through verbatim.
- **X/Twitter** — `handleFromUserLink` accepted any single-segment path, so `twitter.com/home`, `/search`, `/notifications` minted people named `home`, `search`, `notifications`. Those routes are structurally indistinguishable from a profile link, so a reserved-route list is the only thing that can separate them.

Two deliberate scope limits, both load-bearing:

- The reserved check lives in `handleFromUserLink`, **not** in `normalizeXHandle`. A real `@home` / `@intent` account exists; a handle arriving from tweet metadata must survive. Only the *URL reading* is ambiguous.
- `origin_id` still hashes the **original** export fields. Display normalization must not re-mint rows that already exist.

---
name: reference_cli_version_stamp_is_published_not_running_code
description: "cli_version on a run/deployment record reports packages/cli/package.json's PUBLISHED version, not the code that actually ran — a local worktree build stamps the last release"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
---

**`cli_version` on a prod record is not evidence of what code executed.** It is read from `packages/cli/package.json`, which carries the last *published* version. A local build from any worktree — running arbitrary unreleased code — stamps that same published number.

Concretely (2026-08-12): `packages/cli/package.json` says `14.20.0`, published 2026-08-10. Every record produced by a worktree build in the days since also says `cli_version: 14.20.0`, while running code that exists on no release. A peer nearly misread a prod record on this.

So `cli_version: 14.20.0` answers "which release was this package last cut at," never "did my fix run." To establish what actually ran, use a signal derived from the running artifact — a behavior only the new code produces, a log line it uniquely emits, or a SHA carried in the artifact itself.

Same disease as [[reference_deployed_prod_sha_from_image_tag.md]]: the cluster carries no commit, so deployment records report a *published/tagged* identity rather than the executed one. Whenever a provenance field could have been written without the code being present, it is not provenance.

General form: [[feedback_a_wait_condition_that_cannot_report_failure_is_decorative]] — a field that reads the same whether your change is present or absent confirms nothing. Related: [[feedback_verify_dont_reason_from_construction]], [[reference_lobu_cli_runs_dist_not_src]].

content.text:
Decision made on the peer's offer: **gating now rather than waiting for their `ci.yml` fix to merge.** The A/B evidence says uncontended runs pass first try under the *current* ceiling — the 5s ceiling isn't what threatens a solo run, contention is, and they'll be off the machine. Waiting would cost their PR + review + CI + merge of real time to buy headroom I don't need for three serial gates. The concurrency experiment is cleaner as a deliberate run afterward than as something bolted onto my critical path.

Their run is live and my watcher already switched from "wait for a run to appear" to riding it to completion, so the 4-minute timeout resolved itself.

One genuinely useful thing came out of their message, and I've written it to memory: **`cli_version` on a prod record reports the last *published* version, not the code that ran.** `packages/cli/package.json` says `14.20.0` (published 08-10), so any local worktree build stamps `14.20.0` while running unreleased code — they nearly misread a prod record on it. It's the same disease as the deployed-SHA note already in memory: the artifact reports a published identity rather than an executed one. A field that reads identically whether your change is present or absent isn't provenance, which is the same rule as the decorative-check entry I wrote earlier.

Also on record before the experiment runs, which I think is the right way round: they predicted it may still fail for reasons outside their fix, and that this wouldn't retroactively invalidate it. I agreed and won't relitigate that after seeing the result — the probe verifies the 5s fix independently; the experiment tests the separate question of whether two 18-lane graphs can coexist.

Nothing to change in the confidence numbers — no new verification since the last report, just queue position and memory. Still waiting on two notifications: the peer's run exiting, and `review-fix` settling the Maps diff. I'll start gating the moment both clear.

content.content:
---
name: reference_cli_version_stamp_is_not_proof_of_code
description: "cli_version on a prod deployment record reports the PUBLISHED version in package.json, not the code that ran — a local worktree build stamps a release identity while running unreleased code"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: e3e39998-3947-4d70-b1e6-a73e5b005158
  modified: 2026-08-12T17:20:03.149Z
---

`events.metadata->>'cli_version'` on a deployment record is **not evidence of which code produced it.** It is just `packages/cli/package.json`'s `version` field, which sits unbumped between releases. Any local build from a worktree stamps the last published version while running arbitrary unreleased code.

Concretely (2026-08-12): prod carried a deployment record stamped `cli_version: 14.20.0`. 14.20.0 was published 2026-08-10. The record was written 2026-08-12 14:07 UTC and contained the `attribution` + `owned` baseline, a feature that did not exist until #2663 (`05adcd18a`) merged on 08-12. So the published 14.20.0 provably cannot have written it — a local build did, wearing a released version number.

I nearly concluded the feature had shipped to users. It had not.

**Same disease as [[reference_deployed_prod_sha_from_image_tag]]** — the artifact reports a *published* identity rather than the code that ran, and the cluster carries no commit. When you need to know what code produced a prod row, use `git_sha` / `git_dirty` on the same record, or the image tag; never the semver.

Corollary for blast-radius reasoning: "last published version is N, therefore no user has feature X" is only sound if you also confirm no local/unreleased build wrote to that environment. Check `git_sha` against the feature's merge commit.

Related: [[reference_lobu_cli_runs_dist_not_src]] (the sibling trap — the CLI runs `dist`, so editing `src` without rebuilding tests the previous build).

input.content:
## Summary

Adds a `maps` feed to the Google Takeout connector. The archive already sat on disk behind the existing `os.files` device gate — three Maps sources in it were simply never read.

- `Maps (your places)/Saved Places.json` → `saved_place`
- `Maps (your places)/Reviews.json` → `place_review` (rating + answered prompts)
- `Saved/<list>.csv` → `saved_list_place` (starred, want-to-go, favourites, and any custom list)

The three sources disagree with each other in ways that are easy to get wrong, so each trap has a test pinning it:

name: reference_classify_retry_green_by_attempt_1_cause
description: "A Depot run that only goes green on retry is not automatically suspect — classify by attempt-1's NAMED cause into infra / marginal / unknown, and capture attempt ids WHILE the run is live or the evidence is destroyed"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
---

**"Retry-green is unattested" is too coarse.** What matters is whether attempt 1's failure has a cause you can *name*. Three buckets:

1. **Named infra** — network/download/provisioning failures that happen *before any test code runs* (`script exited with code 56` from curl "failed receiving network data"; `Failed to download bun from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/…`; buildx failing to provision the image). **Retry-green is fine.** The code was never exercised, so the retry isn't hiding anything about your diff.
2. **Named marginal** — the `5000.xx ms` gateway-Postgres hook timeouts (`server-integration-bun`, `integration`). **Retry-green is a real warning**: the lane is genuinely near the ceiling and something tipped it. See [[reference_depot_cancelled_lanes_hide_a_real_timeout_failure]].
3. **Unknown cause** — **treat as unattested.** You cannot classify what you cannot read.

Also note lanes that fail only by inheritance: `dead-code-report` has `needs: [… migrations]`, so it reports failed while never having executed. Don't count it as an independent signal.

**`depot ci logs <run>` serves only the LAST attempt.** When a retry succeeds, the passing attempt *overwrites the evidence* — the failed attempt's log becomes unreadable from the CLI, and there is no `--attempt` flag. So a retry-green run silently destroys the only thing that would let you classify it.

**Fix: capture the attempt id while the run is still live.** `depot ci status <run_id>` lists per-attempt ids, and `depot ci logs <attempt-id>` will serve a *failed* attempt directly if you have its id. tail -f "$GATE_OUT" | grep -E --line-buffered "Retrying [0-9]+ failed|failed=|Depot run [a-z0-9]+ (passed|failed)"
```

Do not overstate it. The "same tree contended fails / uncontended passes first try" A/B is **n=2**, and a third run (2026-08-12, uncontended) retried for pure download reasons and fits neither arm.
