2026-08-05: asked to finish a handed-off pi session's PR batch (#2507/#2510/#2516/#2517/#2518), I
ran `make review-fix` + `make review` + merge on all of them — while a **second Claude Code session**
(`claude --dangerously-skip-permissions`, started 13:36) was working the same queue. It merged #2516
between my push and my next `gh pr view`, and had independently posted `pi-review`/`ui-review` on my
head SHA and even prod-verified the reviewer's risk note. Two reviewer passes on the same commit,
paid twice out of a quota that had just come off a limit.

**Why:** PR queues are shared mutable state with no lock. Nothing in `gh` or the worktree tells you a
peer is mid-flight; the first symptom is a PR that merged itself or a status you did not post.

**How to apply:** before starting a multi-PR batch, and again before any force-push or merge:

```bash
ps -eo pid,lstart,command | grep -E "scripts/review\.sh|make review|ui-review\.ts" | grep -v grep
for p in $(pgrep -f "scripts/review.sh"); do lsof -a -p $p -d cwd -Fn | grep ^n; done   # which worktree
```

A `/bin/zsh -c source ~/.claude/shell-snapshots/...` ancestor means another Claude session, not you —
walk `ps -o ppid=` up to the `claude` process and compare its pid to your own tree. Also check
`gh api repos/lobu-ai/lobu/commits/<sha>/statuses --jq '.[] | "\(.context) \(.created_at)"'`: a
status timestamped after your push that you did not post IS a peer.

Use `--force-with-lease` always (it is what stopped me clobbering the peer's work on #2517/#2518),
and surface the collision to the user rather than racing it silently.

**2026-08-12 — the same collision wearing a different mask: Depot gates cancel each other.**
Two of my branches failed `make pre-pr-remote` on the same two lanes (`integration`,
`server-integration-bun`) despite touching disjoint files — one branch changed only
`examples/personal-agent/*.ts`, which cannot reach a server suite. I spent three runs theorising
infra flake. The truth was two OTHER Claude sessions running `make pre-pr-remote` concurrently
(worktrees `apply-plan-values` and one on `/tmp/prepr-r2.log`); concurrent Depot runs supersede and
cancel one another. I then made it worse by starting a `REMOTE_JOBS=` subset in the SAME worktree
while my own full rerun was live, which cancelled my own run.

**`cancelled` NEVER means "contention, safe to rerun".** I wrote that rule here first and it is
wrong — a peer session corrected it within the hour, and
[[reference_depot_cancelled_lanes_hide_a_real_timeout_failure]] (written the SAME DAY, 16:08) already
said so: fail-fast cancels siblings, so the job that genuinely failed also reads `cancelled`. Read
`attempts[]`, never the rolled-up job status:

```sh
depot ci status <run_id> --org "$DEPOT_ORG_ID" --output json \
  | jq -r '.workflows[0].jobs[] | "\(.status)\t\(.job_key)\t\([.attempts[].status]|join(","))"'
```

Contention and a real failure look identical at job level; only the attempt rows separate them.

**And `failed=N` is not reliable either — contention produces hard `failed`, not just `cancelled`.**
I claimed `failed` was the trustworthy signal; a second peer disproved it the same hour. The marginal
lanes are the DB-backed gateway suites — `UserAuthProfileStore > dropAgent cascades through all
secrets`, `OAuthStateStore (Postgres-backed)` (reports as `(unnamed)`), `scanAllOAuth yields every
(userId, agentId, organizationId) triple`. Under load they cross bun's 5s default and report as hard
failures; `integration` then fails downstream as an aggregator.

Instrumented cause (see [[reference_depot_cancelled_lanes_hide_a_real_timeout_failure]] — corrected):
it is NOT the `beforeEach` TRUNCATE (~150ms) and `(unnamed)` is NOT the hook. The cost is the
**`beforeAll` ~1.43s** (embedded Postgres spawn + migrations) charged to the first test. Both this
session and a peer had assumed TRUNCATE and would have shipped a ~100ms saving against a 5s ceiling.
Measuring first is what stopped it.

So neither status distinguishes contention from a real bug. What does:
- **Reachability** — can the diff even import the failing lane? A CLI-only or `examples/`-only diff
  has no path into `packages/server`; that asymmetry is the evidence, not the status.
- **An uncontended rerun** — peer measured same tree contended = failed 4x, uncontended = passed
  first try with NO retry. Rerun uncontended BEFORE bug-hunting, and never conclude either way from a
  contended run.

`depot ci logs --job` wants the **job_key** (`server-integration-bun`), not the job_id.

- `Depot run <id> failed (CLI exit 0)` with `workflow CI: cancelled` — the CLI exits 0, so only the
  marker grep catches it.

```bash
ps -o pid,etime,args -A | grep "[r]un-remote-ci.sh"     # peers holding the slot
```

**The obvious drain-loop is broken — `pgrep -f` SELF-MATCHES.** This cost me a full wait cycle and I
misread it as peers holding the slot:

```bash
until ! pgrep -f "run-remote-ci.sh" >/dev/null; do sleep 20; done   # NEVER goes false
```

`pgrep -f` matches the whole command line and excludes only its OWN pid — not the `zsh -c` wrapper
whose command line *contains the literal pattern string*. So the loop waits on itself forever. A
bounded `for i in $(seq 1 90)` version is worse, not better: it degrades into a fixed 30-minute wait
that looks like patience. Match the real process, not the wrapper:

```bash
while pgrep -af "run-remote-ci.sh" | grep -q "bash \./scripts/run-remote-ci.sh"; do sleep 20; done
```

Ground truth for "is anyone actually gating" — this is what finally showed me two live runs:

```bash
ps -o pid,etime,command -A | grep "[r]un-remote-ci.sh"
```

**Timers cannot resolve a queue; only messages can.** Two sessions both waiting on the same predicate
wake together and re-collide. Agree an explicit order over SendMessage and wait for a "done" message,
not a condition. And a claim can race a start: I began a gate seconds before a peer's claim arrived
and we collided anyway — on discovering that, kill the run whose remaining work is LARGER (I aborted
a full 18-lane run so a peer's cache-hit re-attestation could finish) rather than defending
first-start.

Never run two gates on one branch at once, and never a subset alongside a full run — a subset cannot
attest anyway, so it buys nothing and destroys the run that could.

**2026-08-12 — the queue has a THIRD actor, and PRs merge out from under you.**
A `codex` harness held the Depot slot repeatedly all night from the MAIN
checkout (`codex <- node <- zsh`, cwd `/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu`, no worktree).
Two bumps merged during it: #2705 while a peer was gating the same pin (their PR
came back `DIRTY` on a gitlink conflict), and #2708 **off a branch the peer had
pushed, while that peer's own wait-for-checks loop was still running.**

**You cannot attribute a merge from the API.** Both show `mergedBy: buremba` —
the account, not the actor. Any agent using the user's `gh` token merges as the
user, so `mergedBy` cannot separate the human from a harness, and I was wrong
in both directions on this in one night: first asserting codex had merge rights
at 85% off a `DIRTY` conflict, then retracting it off a `mergedBy` field that
never could have settled it. The only real evidence is a session's first-hand
account that it did not merge its own PR — and even that does not exclude the
human. **Ask the user; do not infer.**

What is certain and is what matters operationally: **a PR can merge while the
session that owns it is still validating.** Re-check `state` immediately before
acting on any PR, not once at the start of a batch.

Consequences for the checks above:
- Walking `ppid` up to a `claude` process is NOT sufficient attribution. A
  `codex` ancestor is an autonomous harness that gates, reviews, AND merges; it
  will not answer a SendMessage and cannot be negotiated with. Plan around it.
- It works from the main checkout, so the "which worktree" `lsof` check returns
  the repo root rather than a task worktree — that is the tell.
- Before starting any bump or queue-wide batch, check the PR is still unmerged
  immediately before acting, not just at the start of the batch.

Related: [[feedback_concurrent_agent_worktree_wipe]], [[feedback_review_is_last_gate_not_the_loop]],
[[reference_depot_cancelled_lanes_hide_a_real_timeout_failure]],
[[feedback_piped_make_exit_code_is_a_false_green]],
[[reference_check_drift_green_can_be_stale_and_lets_a_merge_through]]

| PR | Commit | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| **#2687** | `caf3e9916` | os.files device connectors on a local worker — the original task |
| **#2712** | `c46bccf07` | Fixture isolation + drain timeouts |

**One thing is genuinely not done, and I won't call it finished: #2687 is not in prod.** The watcher is on check 2 and prod is still serving run 2079 / `de158afda6`, which predates the merge. The device-worker credential guard isn't live, so nothing has exercised the path that matters. The watcher runs another ~40 minutes; if the image doesn't roll in that window it'll time out and that check will still be owed. Calling this session "complete" would be the exact false-green pattern that cost us repeatedly tonight.

What actually shipped is small: two test files and one flag per CI lane. The value is that the class is closed — bun's 5000ms default no longer silently fails unrelated tests anywhere in the repo, proven with mutation checks on both files rather than a green run.

Worth naming plainly, since you asked what the long-term fix is and tonight is the evidence: **three PRs took roughly two hours, and almost none of that was the work.** It went to gates and reviews invalidated by things unrelated to the diffs — a concurrency collapse, an owletto bump turning every open PR red, release-please regenerating on every merge. The recommendation stands: make `check-drift` informational for PRs that don't touch `packages/owletto` and let a bot own the bump; put a merge queue in front of main; cache `pi-review` by patch-id so a base-only refresh doesn't burn a review.

I got three things wrong tonight and corrected each: the hook-vs-body timeout diagnosis (refuted by the CI log), "no lane passes `--timeout`" (one did), and "your Postgres is broken" (it's on port 5418). All three came from inferring instead of reading the primary source, and all three are now recorded that way.

content.text:
That closes it — and in the way your own AGENTS rule predicts.

**The deadlock is not reachable in prod.** `expire-pending-approvals` is registered as a cron task, and the scheduler enqueues it with `singletonKey: cronSeedKey(reg.name, tick)` — one job per (task, tick), so multiple pods seeding the same tick collapse into a single execution. The chokepoint already exists; there was nothing to serialize. It runs daily at 03:31, and what I saw was purely a test artifact: bun kept timed-out test bodies running so two sweeps overlapped, which never happens through the real path. **No fix needed** — and adding a lock would have been exactly the mechanism-for-a-misplaced-check your coordination brake warns about.

So, the three items:

tonight I say so, because the wrong version is still plausible-sounding and you
will re-derive it if I don't.

| #2712 | `c46bccf07` | Test fixture isolation + approval-drain timeouts |

concurrency key), #2641 (CLI release 14.21.0).

## TASK 1 — Verify #2687 in prod (the only truly outstanding item)

device-worker credential guard was not live and nothing had exercised it.

`WORKER_API_TOKEN` that is not a durable `owl_pat_` PAT at startup. The
reviewer rated `behavior_change_risk: high`. The failure mode is silent: a
device worker that fails the guard stops polling rather than erroring
somewhere visible, so nobody notices until scheduled `os.files` runs quietly
stop happening.

only join key is the image tag's trailing number, which is the
`Build and Push Images` workflow **run number**:

```bash

TAG=$(kubectl -n summaries-prod get deploy summaries-app-lobu-app \
  -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}')
N=$(echo "$TAG" | sed 's/.*-0*\([0-9]*\)$/\1/')

  --json number,headSha --jq ".[]|select(.number==$N)|.headSha")

```

device worker still authenticates and claims work: it should poll
`/api/workers/poll` with `Authorization: Bearer owl_pat_…` and receive/claim a
run. A worker that has gone quiet is the regression. Checking that the pod is
up is NOT the verification.

work; it was gates and reviews being invalidated by things unrelated to the
diffs. Burak asked for the long-term answer; I consulted codex and we
independently converged on the same top two. Ranked:

### 2a. Stop making `check-drift` a required check on ordinary PRs — do this first
"Pinned to latest `owletto/main`" is volatile global state, not a property of a
lobu change. Today every human commit to owletto/main turns `check-drift` red on
**every** open lobu PR at once, and clearing it requires the branch to actually
take the new base — which invalidates both the Depot tree attestation and the
`pi-review` status, costing a full gate (~6–9 min) plus an LLM review **per PR**.

Target design:
- A scheduled/webhook bot maintains **one coalescing owletto bump PR**.
- That bump PR carries the real validation (commit exists, is reachable from
  `owletto/main`, compatibility E2E).
- Every other PR gets an **informational** drift check only.
- Accept: `lobu/main` may briefly trail owletto. Far cheaper than the current
  invalidation cascade.

`.github/workflows/submodule-drift.yml` already contains the pieces you need —
it exempts FluxCD image commits when **all three** hold: author
`fluxcd@lobu.ai` (`BOT_AUTHOR_EMAIL`, line 27), subject exactly
`chore: update images` (`BOT_SUBJECT`, line 28), and nothing touched outside
`deploy/` (line 118). It also hard-fails when the pinned SHA is not an ancestor
of owletto/main (line 90) — keep that.

### 2b. GitHub merge queue
Nobody merges directly; everyone enqueues. GitHub validates a synthetic commit
of current `main` plus queued changes, which structurally kills stale-green,
stale-red, and author-driven `update-branch` churn. Split the validation:
PR head gets fast tests + `pi-review`; the merge-group SHA gets the
authoritative full Depot attestation. Configure workflows for `merge_group`.
Cost: serial re-testing, so it is throughput-negative when the queue is deep.

### 2c. Cache `pi-review` by normalized patch-id
Codex's idea, and it would have saved the most time tonight. Repost the existing
verdict after a **base-only** refresh; rerun only when the patch actually
changes. A release PR whose content is unchanged and whose base moved currently
burns a full review each time — a peer lost three cycles to exactly this.

It is the biggest hammer and it breaks the deploy path: **Flux reads the owletto
repo's `refs/heads/main` directly**, so owletto code goes live when it merges
there, not when the pin moves. The pain is from the required-check coupling, not
from vendoring. Fix 2a and most of the case for decoupling evaporates.

Seven files share the shared-temp-dir fixture shape that caused the
`credentials.test.ts` cascade, all in `packages/agent-worker/src/__tests__/`:
`embedded-tools`, `system-prompt-delivery`, `bang-bash-session`,
`agent-session-bash-env`, `pi-resource-discovery`, `transcript-snapshot`,
`worker-bash-secret-leak-e2e`.

ever flakes, apply the same pattern as `packages/core/src/__tests__/credentials.test.ts`:
per-test temp dirs, cleanup in `afterAll` (never `afterEach`), explicit timeout
on any I/O-heavy test.

---

**The `expirePendingApprovals` concurrent-sweep deadlock is not reachable in
prod.** I saw `PostgresError: deadlock detected` in a mutated test run and
flagged it. It is a test artifact: bun keeps a timed-out test's async body
running, so two sweeps overlapped.

In prod the chokepoint already exists — `packages/server/src/scheduled/jobs.ts:361`

same tick collapse into one job. Adding a lock would be mechanism papering over
a misplaced check. Leave it.

---

- **bun ignores `timeout` in `bunfig.toml`.** Only the CLI `--timeout` works. A
  config that looks like it raised the ceiling never did.
- **A bun timeout is contagious.** bun does not abort a timed-out test's async
  body; it keeps running and races the next test's fixtures. One slow test was
  measured failing **four unrelated tests**, including pure synchronous ones.
  So a multi-test red can have exactly one cause — check whether the first
  failure is a timeout before believing it is a real regression.
- **Distinguish a hook timeout from a slow body by the STRING, never the
  duration.** `this test timed out after 5000ms` = the body (fix the test);
  `a beforeEach/afterEach hook timed out for this test` = the hook. Both land
  just over 5000ms because that is the ceiling they hit. I got this wrong by
  inferring from durations; the CI log refuted it.
- **`gh run rerun` cannot clear a stale `check-drift`** — a rerun replays the
  same merge ref and reports the old pin no matter how green main is. Use
  `gh pr update-branch`.
- **`mergedBy` cannot attribute a merge.** Every agent uses the same token, so
  it always reads `buremba`. The one discriminator is your own command:
  `gh pr merge … 2>&1; echo "exit=$?"` — exit 0 with no output means you merged
  it; non-zero with `! Pull request #N was already merged` means something beat
  you. A `codex` harness merged three PRs out from under a peer session tonight,
  one of them mid-review. **Re-check `state` immediately before acting.**
- **Never conclude a gate passed from a piped exit code.** `make X 2>&1 | tail`
  reports the pipe's status. Use `make X > log 2>&1; RC=$?; exit $RC`, and read
  the log regardless.
- **Depot: `cancelled` with zero `failed` attempts + `error_message: Cancelled
  due to the workflow concurrency policy` = you were superseded, not a real
  failure.** Rerun; the diff is fine. Exactly one `failed` + N cancelled = a
  real failure, read that attempt's log.
- **Local Postgres is on port 5418, not 5432.** It is not broken. Server tests
  spawn their own embedded Postgres anyway.

Should the `codex` harness merge PRs unattended? It merged three tonight that
other sessions were still validating, including one mid-`pi-review`. That is a
policy decision, not a bug to fix.

# Handoff — lobu, night of 2026-08-12

Everything below is verified unless marked otherwise. Where I was wrong earlier
tonight I say so, because the wrong version is still plausible-sounding and you
will re-derive it if I don't.

## What already landed (do not redo)

| PR | Squash SHA | What |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #2687 | `caf3e9916` | os.files device connectors on a local worker |
| #2712 | `c46bccf07` | Test fixture isolation + approval-drain timeouts |
| #2711 | `6ab5f0d30` | `--timeout 30000` on all 28 `bun test` lanes in `ci.yml` |

Also landed by a peer session: #2704 (bun pin + curl retry), #2707 (CI
concurrency key), #2641 (CLI release 14.21.0).

---

## TASK 1 — Verify #2687 in prod (the only truly outstanding item)

**Status when I handed off: NOT rolled out.** Prod was serving
`ghcr.io/lobu-ai/lobu-app:20260812-223221-002079` → `de158afda62e`, built
22:32:21, which is **four minutes older** than the 22:35:59Z merge. So the
device-worker credential guard was not live and nothing had exercised it.

**Why it matters.** #2687 makes the connector-worker daemon reject any
`WORKER_API_TOKEN` that is not a durable `owl_pat_` PAT at startup. The
reviewer rated `behavior_change_risk: high`. The failure mode is silent: a
device worker that fails the guard stops polling rather than erroring
somewhere visible, so nobody notices until scheduled `os.files` runs quietly
stop happening.

**Step 1 — is it deployed?** Nothing on the cluster carries a commit SHA. The
only join key is the image tag's trailing number, which is the
`Build and Push Images` workflow **run number**:

```bash
MERGE_SHA=$(gh pr view 2687 --json mergeCommit --jq .mergeCommit.oid)   # caf3e9916ef8…
TAG=$(kubectl -n summaries-prod get deploy summaries-app-lobu-app \
  -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}')
N=$(echo "$TAG" | sed 's/.*-0*\([0-9]*\)$/\1/')
DEPLOYED_SHA=$(gh run list --workflow "Build and Push Images" --limit 40 \
  --json number,headSha --jq ".[]|select(.number==$N)|.headSha")
git merge-base --is-ancestor "$MERGE_SHA" "$DEPLOYED_SHA" && echo ROLLED_OUT
```

Two traps, both cost real time before:
- **Merge commit FIRST in `--is-ancestor`.** Reversed, it accepts a stale deploy.
- **Gate on the squash commit, never the branch head.** A squash merge writes a
  new commit with no ancestry to the branch, so a branch-head gate exits 1
  forever and the check silently never opens.
- The three images (`lobu-app`, `lobu-worker`, `lobu-embeddings`) roll
  **independently**; gate on the specific deployment, not "the latest tag".

**Step 2 — once deployed, verify behaviour, not just presence.** Confirm a real
device worker still authenticates and claims work: it should poll
`/api/workers/poll` with `Authorization: Bearer owl_pat_…` and receive/claim a
run. A worker that has gone quiet is the regression. Checking that the pod is
up is NOT the verification.

---

## TASK 2 — The structural CI fix (highest leverage remaining work)

Tonight cost roughly two hours to land ~90 lines. Almost none of that was the
work; it was gates and reviews being invalidated by things unrelated to the
diffs. Burak asked for the long-term answer; I consulted codex and we
independently converged on the same top two. Ranked:

### 2a. Stop making `check-drift` a required check on ordinary PRs — do this first
"Pinned to latest `owletto/main`" is volatile global state, not a property of a
lobu change. Today every human commit to owletto/main turns `check-drift` red on
**every** open lobu PR at once, and clearing it requires the branch to actually
take the new base — which invalidates both the Depot tree attestation and the
`pi-review` status, costing a full gate (~6–9 min) plus an LLM review **per PR**.

Target design:
- A scheduled/webhook bot maintains **one coalescing owletto bump PR**.
- That bump PR carries the real validation (commit exists, is reachable from
  `owletto/main`, compatibility E2E).
- Every other PR gets an **informational** drift check only.
- Accept: `lobu/main` may briefly trail owletto. Far cheaper than the current
  invalidation cascade.

`.github/workflows/submodule-drift.yml` already contains the pieces you need —
it exempts FluxCD image commits when **all three** hold: author
`fluxcd@lobu.ai` (`BOT_AUTHOR_EMAIL`, line 27), subject exactly
`chore: update images` (`BOT_SUBJECT`, line 28), and nothing touched outside
`deploy/` (line 118). It also hard-fails when the pinned SHA is not an ancestor
of owletto/main (line 90) — keep that.

### 2b. GitHub merge queue
Nobody merges directly; everyone enqueues. GitHub validates a synthetic commit
of current `main` plus queued changes, which structurally kills stale-green,
stale-red, and author-driven `update-branch` churn. Split the validation:
PR head gets fast tests + `pi-review`; the merge-group SHA gets the
authoritative full Depot attestation. Configure workflows for `merge_group`.
Cost: serial re-testing, so it is throughput-negative when the queue is deep.

### 2c. Cache `pi-review` by normalized patch-id
Codex's idea, and it would have saved the most time tonight. Repost the existing
verdict after a **base-only** refresh; rerun only when the patch actually
changes. A release PR whose content is unchanged and whose base moved currently
burns a full review each time — a peer lost three cycles to exactly this.

### Do NOT decouple the owletto submodule (yet)
It is the biggest hammer and it breaks the deploy path: **Flux reads the owletto
repo's `refs/heads/main` directly**, so owletto code goes live when it merges
there, not when the pin moves. The pain is from the required-check coupling, not
from vendoring. Fix 2a and most of the case for decoupling evaporates.

---

## TASK 3 — Optional, low priority

Seven files share the shared-temp-dir fixture shape that caused the
`credentials.test.ts` cascade, all in `packages/agent-worker/src/__tests__/`:
`embedded-tools`, `system-prompt-delivery`, `bang-bash-session`,
`agent-session-bash-env`, `pi-resource-discovery`, `transcript-snapshot`,
`worker-bash-secret-leak-e2e`.

All green today (111–753ms locally), and #2711 raised the ceiling to 30s beneath
them repo-wide, which removes the trigger. **I would leave these alone.** If one
ever flakes, apply the same pattern as `packages/core/src/__tests__/credentials.test.ts`:
per-test temp dirs, cleanup in `afterAll` (never `afterEach`), explicit timeout
on any I/O-heavy test.

---

## DO NOT "FIX" — investigated and closed

**The `expirePendingApprovals` concurrent-sweep deadlock is not reachable in
prod.** I saw `PostgresError: deadlock detected` in a mutated test run and
flagged it. It is a test artifact: bun keeps a timed-out test's async body
running, so two sweeps overlapped.

In prod the chokepoint already exists — `packages/server/src/scheduled/jobs.ts:361`
registers it as a cron task (`31 3 * * *`), and `task-scheduler.ts:385` enqueues
with `singletonKey: cronSeedKey(reg.name, tick)`, so multiple pods seeding the
same tick collapse into one job. Adding a lock would be mechanism papering over
a misplaced check. Leave it.

---

## Traps that cost time tonight — read before you start

- **bun ignores `timeout` in `bunfig.toml`.** Only the CLI `--timeout` works. A
  config that looks like it raised the ceiling never did.
- **A bun timeout is contagious.** bun does not abort a timed-out test's async
  body; it keeps running and races the next test's fixtures. One slow test was
  measured failing **four unrelated tests**, including pure synchronous ones.
  So a multi-test red can have exactly one cause — check whether the first
  failure is a timeout before believing it is a real regression.
- **Distinguish a hook timeout from a slow body by the STRING, never the
  duration.** `this test timed out after 5000ms` = the body (fix the test);
  `a beforeEach/afterEach hook timed out for this test` = the hook. Both land
  just over 5000ms because that is the ceiling they hit. I got this wrong by
  inferring from durations; the CI log refuted it.
- **`gh run rerun` cannot clear a stale `check-drift`** — a rerun replays the
  same merge ref and reports the old pin no matter how green main is. Use
  `gh pr update-branch`.
- **`mergedBy` cannot attribute a merge.** Every agent uses the same token, so
  it always reads `buremba`. The one discriminator is your own command:
  `gh pr merge … 2>&1; echo "exit=$?"` — exit 0 with no output means you merged
  it; non-zero with `! Pull request #N was already merged` means something beat
  you. A `codex` harness merged three PRs out from under a peer session tonight,
  one of them mid-review. **Re-check `state` immediately before acting.**
- **Never conclude a gate passed from a piped exit code.** `make X 2>&1 | tail`
  reports the pipe's status. Use `make X > log 2>&1; RC=$?; exit $RC`, and read
  the log regardless.
- **Depot: `cancelled` with zero `failed` attempts + `error_message: Cancelled
  due to the workflow concurrency policy` = you were superseded, not a real
  failure.** Rerun; the diff is fine. Exactly one `failed` + N cancelled = a
  real failure, read that attempt's log.
- **Local Postgres is on port 5418, not 5432.** It is not broken. Server tests
  spawn their own embedded Postgres anyway.

## Open question for Burak (not an agent task)

Should the `codex` harness merge PRs unattended? It merged three tonight that
other sessions were still validating, including one mid-`pi-review`. That is a
policy decision, not a bug to fix.
